summary: All three FEAT acceptance criteria are met. FEAT-001: Navbar.jsx has isAuthority guard (sub-admin/super-admin) using hyphenated role strings that match the backend USER_ROLES enum; Sidebar.jsx bottom CTA is wrapped in {!isAuthority && (...)}; MyReports.jsx was not touched. FEAT-002: useVoiceToText.js exists with correct API (isListening, transcript, start, stop, supported); ReportIssue.jsx appends transcript via useEffect (not replaces); mic+lang selector only renders when voiceSupported. FEAT-003: slaEscalation.js exports both checkSLABreaches and startSlaWorker; no mongoose.connect in checkSLABreaches body; server.js calls startSlaWorker() after app.listen(); both files pass node --check. Two non-blocking observations: (1) no bare 'admin' role guard — unlikely to matter today but worth documenting; (2) page-level buttons in MyReports.jsx/Feed.jsx were explicitly descoped by FEAT-001 and may still expose the button to authority users from those pages.
findings: No 'admin' role in isAuthority guard — USER_ROLES enum has no bare 'admin' today so not a current bug, but adding it defensively prevents a silent miss if the role is introduced later.
Page-level Report Issue buttons in MyReports.jsx and Feed.jsx were descoped by FEAT-001 and remain unguarded — confirm whether those buttons exist and track for a follow-up task.
